name: acceptance
quote: The bad news didn't seem to bother her at all.
description: Reacting to an unchangeable and unpleasant situation with authentic calmness and without significant complaint.
perceptions: I would have preferred a different outcome.
There's not much point in worrying too much about it.

guidance.description: Here are some references that may help become more accepting of things you can't change.
If you feel like you're too accepting, see the guidance for 'agreeableness'.

variations.name: agreement
variations.description: Confirming that you're willing to let an outcome proposed by someone else to happen.
perceptions: I can choose to allow it to happen or reject it.
This outcome is fine with me.
examples: Saying 'I do' to a wedding vow.
Signing a release waiver for skydiving.

variations.name: unhappy acceptance
variations.description: Reacting to the reality of an undesired outcome with a sense of loss, but not trying to change it.
perceptions: I would have much preferred a different outcome.
But I can't change this outcome.
I will unfortunately need to get used to this one.
examples: Moving on after losing the championship.

guidance.description: See guidance for the various forms of loss.

commentaries.quote: The experiences driven by acceptance and agreement can range from very positive to very negative. The trick is in knowing when it's appropriate to resist and disagree.
Acceptance of what has happened is the first step to overcoming the consequences of any misfortune.
The acceptance of certain realities doesn’t preclude idealism. It can lead to certain breakthroughs.
God, grant me the serenity to accept the things I cannot change, the courage to change the things I can, and the wisdom to know the difference.
What we call reality is an agreement that people have arrived at to make life more livable.
